description: Hi! I’m a multidisciplinary problem-solver fascinated by science and the universe—from the quantum level to the cosmos. With knowledge spanning physics, medicine, science, and technology, my core strength is quickly analyzing complex challenges in deep detail and turning difficult problems into simple, creative, and practical solutions.
summary:
I developed SPHEREx Observatory, an interactive web prototype designed to democratize astronomical data exploration and accelerate celestial discovery. Leveraging Google AI Studio to overcome coding barriers and streamline problem-solving, I built an intuitive interface that empowers users to identify planets, stars, and comets quickly and effectively.

This project tackles the steep learning curve of interpreting complex space mission datasets through an interactive multi-layer visualization and spectral analysis system. By translating raw spectral data into an accessible visual format, the platform creates a welcoming, educational environment for beginners while simultaneously streamlining workflows for experienced researchers.

The impact of this initiative lies in bridging the gap between citizen science and professional astronomy. Built with a vision of continuous, user-driven interface improvement, SPHEREx Observatory turns complex space observation into an engaging, collaborative experience—fostering scientific curiosity and enabling anyone to contribute to new discoveries across the cosmos.
dataRefs: To understand the complexity of the platform's web data engine, it is imperative to analyze the optical and thermomechanical nature of the data generated by the observatory. Unlike conventional space telescopes, such as the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) or Hubble, which use narrow-field spectrographs or discrete photometric filters, the SPHEREx spacecraft acquires its data using Linear Variable Filters (LVF) technology 1 .

The mission's primary data are not simple images, but highly structured photometric and spectral files called Spectral Image Multi-Extension FITS (MEF) 1 . Access is completely anonymous, allowing the web interface to consume data streams without requiring cumbersome authentication (--no-sign-request in CLI protocols) 1 . Instead of transferring the entire MEF file, the Node.js-based backend server issues Byte-range HTTP requests. This approach emulates the capabilities of modern cloud-optimized formats like Zarr 2 .

The Gaia DR3 astrometric data model consists of a five- or six-parameter solution (spanning position, parallax, proper motion, and, for select stars, the astrometrically estimated effective wavenumber) 1 . The catalog mathematically defines the motion of stars through proper motion vectors in right ascension ($\mu_{\alpha*} \equiv \mu_\alpha \cos\delta$) and declination ($\mu_\delta$), measured in milliarcseconds per year (mas/yr) and calculated under local tangent plane projections 2 .

The Canadian Near-Earth Object Surveillance Satellite (NEOSSat) introduces a fundamental Solar System component to the infrared interface. Jointly funded by the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) and Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC), NEOSSat is a suitcase-sized microsatellite launched in 2013 on an Indian PSLV-C20 rocket 1 . Orbiting 800 kilometers above the Earth with a 100-minute period, its 15 cm Maksutov telescope is not limited by weather cycles or the Earth's atmosphere 2 .
projectRefs: This mathematical algorithmic foundation is critical: the layers do not float randomly when the viewer zooms or pans the matrix; the ESA, CSA, and IRSA sets orbit harmonically around the gnomonic center tied to the screen

Level 01 (Proper Motion: Barnard's Star): The user navigates to the stellar system with the highest proper motion in the sky. There, they must use the Web Worker "|A - B| Subtraction" mode to notice an unmistakable astrometric jump to the north against the immovable bed of surrounding static stars, cross-checking the phenomenon with the cyan kinematic arrow from ESA's Gaia satellite 1 .

To circumvent catastrophic overlap, the backend POST /api/report route was developed without direct immediate transactional operations against final persistent storage (Persistence Storage S3/JSON Disk Store). Instead, each citizen report slides into an asynchronous FIFO (First-In, First-Out) queue hosted purely in the Express 4 cluster's shared RAM. Subsequently, a single-threaded worker gradually extracts one report after another and evaluates its viability by cross-checking it against the reportValidation.ts engine 1
